utterances.speaker: ZELJKO GLASNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, as I mentioned before in the beginning of the interview or my testimony, I understood that he came from, I believe, Germany, that he was one of the founders of the so-called "Kaznjenicka Bojna." I knew he was respected in Siroki Brijeg, and that he partook in the early battles in Mostar in 1992, and that's -- that's about the limit of my knowledge, and also, in -- another is that he was under surveillance in the previous system from the previous internal security apparatus as an immigrant, as part of the Croatian immigration.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Well, sir, I'm going to ask this only because the answer you just gave and I want to make that clear, didn't Mr. Naletilic at that time have a widespread reputation for being a terrorist?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO GLASNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Again, I have no -- what you mean by terrorist or I have no idea what you mean by that statement, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: That he'd been involved in political bombings and killings in various places in the world?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes? Well, Mr. Krsnik.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I would like to know the foundation for such an utterance. Do we have any sentence, and what is the source for the Prosecution of this knowledge, because otherwise, I will say that the Prosecution is setting up.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Scott, we are a little bit surprised by the term "terrorist," "political bombings" and "killings around various places in the world."

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: I'll answer your question, Your Honour, and the witnesses, I was very careful to say, the only reason I'm saying this is because of the answer that the witness gave and he tried in my opinion, I respectfully submit to the Chamber, to suggest that there was some bad reason why he might, and assuming it's true, might have been under surveillance by the previous government. That's why I followed it up with the question I did. As to the answer to Mr. Krsnik's question, it is based upon repeated news interviews given by Mr. Naletilic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Could I comment on my statement?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, yes, you may do that.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It's a well known fact that the former Yugoslav internal security service, the UDBA waged a war against Croatian emigres, from 1945 until 1990, in which approximately 90 Croatians were assassinated abroad. I mentioned this fact because I myself saw a list, an UDBA list, on which Mr. Naletilic was mentioned and the agents that were appointed to track his movements, but not as far as I know a terrorist, but as a political activist.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: Mr. Scott, you and I come from the same legal background. Do you think that this evidence would be allowed either at home or in my country? Would it not be attacked for being more prejudicial than probative and wouldn't you get your knuckles rightly smacked by the trial judge.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: No, Your Honour, I don't believe so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: Certainly in my country you would be in big trouble.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: I respect that, Your Honour. I've never practised, I'm sad to say, I've never practised in Ireland. Maybe some day I'll have the opportunity.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: It certainly sounds like something that is more prejudicial than probative and I think in the interests of justice you should not proceed with it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And I did not intend to, Judge Clark, on that part I can assure you we are in agreement.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Sir, you had known of him, but again as you told us, you did not meet him until sometime perhaps as early as or late as early 1994; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO GLASNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The first conversation we had that lasted more than five minutes was at his -- by swimming pool in Siroki Brijeg in the summer of 1994. Or excuse me, 1995, I meant to say.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And what was the occasion?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO GLASNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the time I was forming the 1st Guards Brigade in Capljina. We had passed -- I had passed through the town of Siroki Brijeg on the way to Tomislavgrad, to visit my 3rd Battalion and we met an individual that knew Mr. Naletilic from the Siroki Brijeg Battalion, the number 1 Battalion, and we went up for a visit.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: When you say you went up to a visit, you went up to a visit where?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO GLASNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: To his house which overlooks Siroki Brijeg.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: You also testified, if I heard you correctly, sir, that you were not aware of Tuta having a military function. Did I hear you correctly?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO GLASNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I said before, the only direct contact I had with members or parts of the unit of the so-called Kaznjenicka Bojna was during the summer or late fall of 1995, when they were part of my defence line holding against Republika Srpska on the Glamoc battlefield.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Sir, I'm not going to ask you at that point about 1995, at least at this point in time. You had no other dealings with him as you've told us then, you can't say anything more about him or his role prior to January 199-- or early 1994; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO GLASNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In any detail, apart from what I said, I can't add anything really.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: All right. During the time period, sir, from late 1992 to early 1994, were you ever present at the Convicts Battalion headquarters?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO GLASNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was not.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: You know where that headquarters was located?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO GLASNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The main headquarters, the -- which headquarters are you --

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Main headquarters of the Convicts Battalion, if you know?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO GLASNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not know. I assumed it was either in Siroki or Mostar.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: During the period from late 1992 to early 1994, did you ever attend or participate in any command meetings of the Convicts Battalion?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO GLASNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Any which meetings?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Commands, briefings, planning sessions, meetings of the commanders of the Convicts Battalion?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO GLASNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you repeat the time period again, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: From late 1992 to early 1994.

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO GLASNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At this time I can't recall that I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Did you ever attend any after-action debriefings at the Convicts Battalion?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO GLASNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Were you ever --

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO GLASNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Excuse me, you mean an after-action review, after an operation?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Yes, sir?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO GLASNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Were you ever present at any time when discipline was imposed in connection with a member of the Convicts Battalion?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO GLASNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't -- I distinctly don't know of which case you're speaking of, but I had individuals in my brigade that had crossed over from the Convicts Battalion to my brigade. I had several such individuals.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Who were they?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO GLASNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was a Canadian and I believe another fellow. I know I know them by name.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: The name of the Canadian, please?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO GLASNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Ronnie Persera. [phoen]

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And the other -- any other men you can tell us, names you can give us?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO GLASNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There maybe a German, but again, both of these individuals were killed in 1994, and one in 1994 and one in 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And the name of the German, please?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO GLASNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We called him Bismarck.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: At what time did they join your unit coming from the Convicts Battalion?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO GLASNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Bismarck joined the unit in the King Tomislav Brigade in the -- he was killed in Uskoplje in 1993 and he joined in, I believe, mid-1993 and Ronnie Persera [phoen] joined the 1st Guards Brigade in Capljina in the spring of 1994. He was killed in Kupres that same year.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: All right. But he did not make any transfer to your knowledge from the Convicts Battalion until sometime in the spring of 199-- I'm sorry, spring of 1994?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO GLASNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean Mr. Persera [phoen] or the -- yes, Mr. Persera [phoen], yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Okay. All right. Just to go back because perhaps my question wasn't clear, sir, apart from these two men coming to your unit later, were you ever present at any time when an existing member of the Convicts Battalion was disciplined in any way by the command of the Convicts Battalion?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO GLASNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't recall such an incident.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Sir, you and your unit, as you told us yesterday, were directly engaged in the fighting around Gornji Vakuf or as you called it, Uskoplje, in 1993, correct?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO GLASNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Parts of the unit were engaged there, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Were you engaged there?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO GLASNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was engaged in the peace talks and in the outset of the conflict.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Well --

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO GLASNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: But in actual fighting I was not engaged.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: All right. Where were you physically located at the time that fighting was going on?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO GLASNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At times I was in Prozor. At times some of the surrounding villages visiting members of my unit that were attached to the operational group that was there, and at other times I was in Tomislavgrad.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Sir, I've been reminded to ask you, so let me backtrack for one moment. You said at one point yesterday you had no knowledge of Tuta having a military function and, yet, if not yesterday at least today, you've said that you knew that he was involved in the battles around Mostar in 1992. Now, what did you know about that?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO GLASNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As one of the founders of the Convicts Battalion, I assumed that's where he'd started his military career or his -- I was told he was one of the founders of the Convicts Battalion.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Who told you that?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO GLASNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The exact individual, the time and the place, I can't recall.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And who told you that he was involved in the liberation of Mostar in 1992?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO GLASNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It could have been Ivan Andabak oar Romeo Cavar or any of the other members of the 22nd -- the Resumski Oderid [phoen] Commando Sector or section.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Just so the record is clear, wouldn't it be fair to say contrary to what you said yesterday you have no knowledge of his having a military function, in fact you did know that he did have a military function at least in the spring and summer of 1992?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO GLASNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Again, I say it's for -- his role in the founding of the battalion to me was not clear.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Well, what were -- we have moved back just a moment, let me ask you this: You've said that Mr. Naletilic was respected in Siroki Brijeg. What was his role in Siroki Brijeg at that time?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO GLASNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Again, as I say, having not been a member of the municipal government there, or the Domobran unit that was stationed there, I can only assume that his management skills, which he learned overseas, his numerous contacts which he probably had, he was a businessman, that he -- he contributed to the defence of the town, it's more the town itself, because I believe the majority of the members from the unit were basically from Siroki Brijeg, and Western Herzegovina so again I can only assume that he had talents that could be used in a positive manner in the defence of his town and community.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: When you said experience and talent, you mean that could be used in -- you mean military and fighting experience, correct?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO GLASNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, as far as I know, sir, he is he is not a soldier and he does not have a pedigree. I don't know what unit he served in.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Sir, I didn't say formal military training, and we spent a lot of time talking about training or the lack thereof. He had fighting experience that you thought you assumed could be helpful to the cause, correct?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO GLASNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Again, my impression of Mr. Naletilic, which I learned -- which I based my observations on, is that he was more or less a logistician, an administrator and a man who worked hand in hand with the municipal government in Siroki Brijeg.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: What do you base that on, sir?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO GLASNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: From speaking to him about certain topics.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: At times, after the beginning of 1994, right?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO GLASNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I said, yes, when I met him in the first conversation was at the change of command and the second was in the summer of 1994, I'm sorry, 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: The full -- you've been very careful to say you want to base your testimony on direct knowledge, so the full scope of your direct knowledge in this regard is based on two conversations with Mr. Naletilic, both after early 1994; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO GLASNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think, sir, you're asking me that if I know whether Mr. Naletilic was an operational or tactical commander in a military unit. All I can say to that question is that I've never seen him in a military uniform or on a confrontation line.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And that's exactly it, sir, isn't it, you don't know one way or the other. The only thing you can tell this Chamber is that you haven't seen him on a confrontation line in a military uniform, correct?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO GLASNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That assumption is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Who was the overall -- going back, and forgive me for the detour, sir, going back to Gornji Vakuf, were you there and can you tell the Chamber who was the overall commander of the HVO forces in connection with the fighting at Gornji Vakuf in January, 1993?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO GLASNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: For that time period, Zeljko Siljeg was the zone commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Do you know at that time who Mr. Siljeg was reporting to as his superior?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO GLASNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Again, it would have been the main headquarters, Mr. Petkovic or Mr. Praljak or whoever was appointed by those two men whoever they delegated authority to.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Do you recall sir what other HVO units were engaged in that fighting in addition to yours?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO GLASNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The order of battle is such formally, I can't name every unit but I can mention some. The parts of the King Tomislav Brigade, the Domobran Brigades from Prozor, Gornji Vakuf, and with all certainty, that's all I can say for -- that I saw when I -- when I toured the line were those units, because Prozor was the main logistics base and the tactical command centre of the HVO at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Sir, isn't it correct that Tuta's unit fought along side your unit in the fighting in Gornji Vakuf in January of 1993?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO GLASNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That, sir, I do not know.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Well, sir, you told us before the last break that one of the most important things was to know who was on your left and who was on your right?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO GLASNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The brigade I'm speaking of, I had two platoons, deployed in the villages of Drenjski [phoen], Orasje, and parts of armoured battalion. They were in direct control of the commander on the terrain and he used them as his asset. That commander it then was Zeljko Siljeg in that zone.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: All right, sir, I'm sorry I'm looking at the transcript and I didn't get the names and I apologise, the names of those three villages but can you assist me, please, and more importantly assist the Judges. The first village you mentioned what was the name again?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO GLASNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Orasje.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And which of your forces or deputy commanders were in charge or located around Orasje?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO GLASNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That would have been a platoon commanded by so-called "Schwabo."

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Can you spell that name for the record, please?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO GLASNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's an abbreviation, it's S-C-H-W-A-B-0.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Do you know his full name?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO GLASNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Ivan Stanic.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: What was his position?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO GLASNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was a commander at the time of a special platoon formed for intervention.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And who was his direct superior, sir?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO GLASNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the time, he was part of the -- an overall unit that originated from the MUP, which was the civilian police, and his commander at the time was another nickname, Kule.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Kula?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO GLASNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Kule, as far as I know.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And his full name, if you know?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO GLASNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'll recall it in a minute if you give me time. Last name was Jurilj.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Sir, unless we misunderstood each other my question was, your forces, so can you take us to what point why these forces were they subordinate to you?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO GLASNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were -- the battle in Gornji Vakuf took place for a month. It lasted for a month and it ended at approximately somewhere in early February. And over that time period, certain units were sent and rotated from that area. The last unit that was there in the town of Uskoplje itself, in the centre of the town before the ceasefire was the Kupres, parts of the Kupres Battalion, and the commander was Krsto.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: If I could ask the witness please to be shown Exhibit 235.2, if you can put the English on the ELMO, please? Sir, on the 1st of January, excuse me, my mistake, on the 26th of January, 1993, did you not issue an order or a request quote for all weapons seized in Gornji Vakuf by Tuta's unit to be returned to Tomislavgrad and put in use at the front lines over the command of commander of King Tomislav Brigade, Colonel Zeljko Glasnovic?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO GLASNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, this order I don't recall, nor do I recall the reason why I would write such an order or a request. There is no signature here, I believe.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Sir, there wouldn't be a signature on an electronic communication, would there?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO GLASNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If a request is sent, to authorise this request here, I would delegate a member of my staff and I made a point of this, I would delegate authority anywhere I'd sign his name so I could identify who signed the document. I see no signature here. A delegate from headquarters is a representative of the commander and I did this to avoid abusing the system, because it was abused.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] Could I ask that the witness please be shown Exhibit -- this is previously -- I don't believe it's in the bundle. It was previously admitted but I do have a couple of extra copies here. One can be put -- it's Exhibit 221.1.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the booths get a copy as well, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: I just you put it on the ELMO. If you put it on the ELMO, I'll be very brief, but --

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Sir, this appears to be a report from the 18th of January, 1993, coming from Gornji Vakuf and HVO officer named Ivan Kraljevic and directing your attention to about the middle of the document, does it not say "it was reported that two members of the Convicts Battalion were killed in the village of Uskoplje today," which is the very village, the very village that you told us about a moment ago where your units were engaged?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO GLASNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I had two people killed there and they were members of the Tomislav brigade, from what I know, not the Kaznjenicka Bojna.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Well, sir, I won't argue with you that perhaps you did have members of your brigade killed there, unfortunately. Does not this report indicate that there were also two members of the Convicts Battalion killed around that same time in that same location?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO GLASNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I said, I know the general outcome of the fighting in Gornji Vakuf, but the task organisation in that sector, I -- different phases of the battle I can't say with any certainty. The line shifted, I know the relay which you're speaking of here was taken, because I was there after it was taken and I know my engineer was there to disarm the mines, but I can't say with any certainty which units were there at the time. As I say the battle lasted for a month.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Sir, you cannot say with any certainty that the Convicts Battalion was not involved at Gornji Vakuf, can you?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO GLASNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can say neither positively nor negatively whether they were there.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And it's also true, is it not, sir, you cannot say either positively or negatively, if Mr. Naletilic was commanding those troops when they were engaged in Gornji Vakuf in January of 1993, correct?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO GLASNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Did you ever have a subordinate officer called Ivan Brago?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO GLASNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The name is not familiar to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: All right. How did you come to be engaged, you and your unit, how did you come to be engaged in the area of Sovici Doljani in April 1993?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO GLASNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The fighting had broken out again, the situation had escalated, and we took over our defence line as I mentioned before, that was established sometime towards the end of April.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Can you tell us who ordered -- what superior officer ordered your assignment or disposition?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO GLASNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was Zeljko Siljeg, I believe it was on the spot when we took the line over.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And was there a HVO officer around this time also named Mico Lasic?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO GLASNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the time that they took the line over.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Well, around, in April 1993, was there another HVO officer in that general area called Mico Lasic?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO GLASNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, there was not.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Do you know a Mico Lasic?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO GLASNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Who was he?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO GLASNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was earlier the commander or zone commander, sometime in Mostar, I believe.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: What time?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO GLASNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: During -- from start -- I'm sure he -- he changed roles with General Obradovic or Mr. Obradovic, but for that time period he was a zone commander at one time or another from 1992 to 1994 of Mostar.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Are you telling us, sir, that sometime, is it correct, that are you saying that he was the head of the defence zone in Mostar continuously from 1992 to 1994 or sometime during that period?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO GLASNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Those details to me are not clear. I know he was there generally. The direct dealings I had with Mico Lasic were in Kupres for the Jajce operation, where he was wounded on part of the line that my troops held in the fall of 1994.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Sir, there were operative zones, the HVO was organised according to various operative zones, correct?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO GLASNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, four operative zones which were formed in late 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And the commander for example of the Central Bosnia operative zone was Tihomir Blaskic, the commander of the northwest operative zone was Mr. Siljeg, and who was commander of the southwest zone?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO GLASNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Again, as I said, command changed, I think between Mr. Lasic and Mr. Obradovic. Mr. Obradovic was towards the end of, I believe, 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: So in early 1993 from what you're telling us it's likely that Mr. Lasic had that position, correct?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO GLASNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: From dispatches it would seem so, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: If I could have the usher's assistance in showing, and again, it may not have been in the bundles, Your Honour, and my apologies, Exhibit 299.1. Mr. Usher? I -- Madam Registrar, I don't believe you'll have it, you can check, but I think it may have been omitted. 299.1. It's a prior -- my apologies. It's a prior exhibit. It wasn't in my bundle is what I meant to say. My apology. It wasn't in the bundle but it's a previous exhibit in the case. If that could be placed on the ELMO, please?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the booths have the document as well, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Of course. If one of the extra copies or some of the extra copies I just tendered could be given to the booths, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Sir, is it not correct that as reflected by Exhibit P299.1, previously admitted in this case, an order was issued on the 15th of April, 1993, quote, "Pursuant to the agreement with commander of the southwest zone of the Herzegovina or HZ," I'll simply just say HZ community, "Brigadier Mico Lasic; with coordinator for Herceg-Bosna, Mladen Naletilic, Tuta; representative of the Main Staff, Colonel Ivan Andabak; I, issue, hereby the following order, PDV platoon and reconnaissance squad are to be on 15 April, 1993 at 1000 hours in the area of Sovicka Vrata." Do you recall that order, sir?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO GLASNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not recall this order.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Isn't it true, sir, that in fact, not only the Convicts Battalion but Mr. Naletilic himself personally was engaged in the fighting around Doljani and Sovici in mid-April and following, 1993?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO GLASNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There is a problem with this document I would just like to point out.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO GLASNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The first, the Posusje Battalion was not an organic unit of the King Tomislav Brigade. They were --

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Perhaps you better tell the Chamber what an organic unit is?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO GLASNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were not in the structure of the HVO brigade at this time that this order was written, 15/04/93. They were detached to the area of Konjic in the third month by Zeljko Siljeg. And I find it inconceivable that if they were part of an organic part of a King Tomislav Brigade that the commander of the battalion, Ivan Brago would sign this order without my knowledge.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Sir, you told us a few minutes ago in connection with Gornji Vakuf that units were coming and going all the time and different units would be detached and different units would be subordinated and they would come and go, and yet you told us in connection with Gornji Vakuf that were you the superior officer of those units, correct?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO GLASNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This was not the manner in which I worked or which -- the way I delegated authorities.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Sir, apart from the document, I come back to the question I put to you and I put it to you again, isn't it true, sir, that Mladen Naletilic, Tuta, and his unit, the Convicts Battalion, were engaged in the fighting in Sovici Doljani in mid-April, 1993?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO GLASNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The date for the taking of not Doljani, but Sovici, proceeded the arrival of our brigade to that sector.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: When did you arrive in that sector?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO GLASNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The third week of April or the end of April.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And you're telling the Chamber then that you don't know what happened in the previous several weeks of fighting in Sovici Doljani, again one way or the other?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO GLASNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I took the line over towards the end of April, the Jajce Brigade, which was mentioned in one of your reports was on my left. On my right was an unit from Siroki Brijeg, the Domobran unit or the home guard unit. And to their right was the Mijat Tomic Battalion and on that line which I already stated which stretched from Kucani on the left to Strop on the right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, the witness has repeatedly said that Domobran, the home guard unit from Siroki Brijeg. Now I look at this, it is never translated. A home guard unit means -- can the interpreters help?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: I'm sorry I only interrupt because I don't want the testimony coming from counsel. If the interpreters can assist us, that's fine and, of course, if the witness can answer it, that's also fine.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Krsnik, you may raise that issue but we want to hear the answer from the witness or some corrections from the interpreters.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, of course, Your Honours. As you see, I made only two objections today. I disrupted in no way the proceedings. And far be it from me. But the objections from the Prosecutor, Your Honours, I will not allow. I will not allow objections on my account. Because we've broken any communication with Mr. Scott and Mr. Stringer any way. And you've heard this comment too, haven't you?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, we don't have the time to debate on that issue. Shall we move on, Mr. Scott?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: Perhaps the witness will tell us what a home guard brigade is. Sorry, unit.

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO GLASNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The home guard units was the unit based in the town from which it originated from the inhabitants of that town, based on the previous territorial system of the JNA.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: My knowledge of military matters, I think is perfectly obviously limited but I understood that a home guard brigade are usually older, non-combat troops, men over 45 or something like that. Am I wrong about that.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. The assumption is not correct. The King Tomislav Brigade was a home guard unit. The nomenclature was changed in 1994. They went from brigades -- There was a restructuring but they were the basis of the -- before the professional formation of professional brigades in the HVO the four professional brigades, they were the backbone of defence of the HVO and they employed all members of military age. If I can just comment on the use of these brigades, younger men were used in offensive actions and older men were used usually for holding a line. And basically, the whole municipality was engaged from -- and all resources within that municipality were poured into the brigade which means tactical sustainment depended on the municipal level which changed later in 1994 when logistics bases were formed at the zone level.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Could the witness please be shown Exhibit 301.1?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Sir, this is an interim report by Mr. or Colonel Siljeg, your superior or the 16th of April, 1993 and I direct your attention to the middle of the second page, or in any event, item numbered 7, not your superior, Mr. Siljeg, report coordinating with Tuta is being done through the Posusje unit on Sovicka Vrata.

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO GLASNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Do you wish an answer?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO GLASNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I said, the Posusje unit was not an organic part of the King Tomislav Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: That was not my question, sir, I don't think I asked you that?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO GLASNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not too sure of your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Didn't your superior, sir, by this communication, indeed reflect that Tuta and his unit was involved in the action at Sovici Doljani in April, 1993.

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO GLASNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The man that can best answer that question is Zeljko Siljeg.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And you have no information to the contrary; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO GLASNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: My information of the placement of the Posusje Battalion or it was not a battalion then at that time, was in the municipality of Konjic, and I understand they were there for the majority of the third month, of the third month and a good part of the fourth month of 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Can you tell us who Mile Curic was, please?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO GLASNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Could you tell us who he was?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO GLASNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was a staff officer in the operative zone of Herzegovina -- Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Where was he based?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO GLASNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, originally he was in my brigade, the King Tomislav Brigade and after the formation of the zones, he was redeployed to the Prozor tactical headquarters as a staff member in the G3 section.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: What's G3?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO GLASNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Operations section of the zone.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: What's the abbreviation or letters chief of ONO stand for?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO GLASNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Literally, that means the officer responsible for operational -- operational order writing, reporting and so on. He organises the G3 sector, the headquarters staff in any operation reports and carries on other duties assigned to him by the commander which is Zeljko Siljeg.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: I ask the witness please be shown Exhibit P469. Sir, this is a regular combat report coming from indeed the headquarters in Prozor on the 20th of June, 1993, from Mile Curic and in his paragraph number 2, our forces, does he not report, "At about 1600 hours, Tuta launched an attack in the sector of Boksevica, with the support of our units holding positions." It goes on to say in about the middle of that paragraph, this was on the basis of radio communications between Tuta and his men that we heard. Continuing through the paragraph, "While Tuta targeted Jablanica, we provided support with our artillery as needed and as requested by Tuta." Now, that's what Mr. Curic, exactly the officer, in exactly the place that you put him -- said, correct?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO GLASNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's the correct translation of this report I have in my hand.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And you have no information to the contrary, do you, sir?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO GLASNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have none to the contrary.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Sir, it was widely known, I put it to you it was widely known, it was known to you, that the Convicts Battalion was Tuta's unit, that they were Tuta's men, often known as "Tutici," that Tuta was in command of them and the HVO Minister of Defence knew it, Colonel Siljeg knew it, Mr. Curic knew it and you knew it, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Krsnik?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm sorry, Your Honours, it may be common knowledge to the Prosecutor, but I'm afraid it is not common knowledge accessible anyone else so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: I think he has to answer that, not you, Mr. Krsnik.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm objecting.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: You cannot object to.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm not going to answer. I want to object and say that one cannot exam somebody about the generally known facts, same thing as Mr. Par objected to earlier. That is all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Mr. Krsnik, he's putting in my view a perfectly reasonable and permitted answer -- question in cross-examination. The witness can respond negatively or positively but he's permitted to put it, having laid the ground.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Sir, it was known to you and by a number of senior HVO officers, whom you identified and testified about at length, it was known to them and it was known to you that the Convicts Battalion was Tuta's unit, correct?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO GLASNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The names you've mentioned, the names you've mentioned, the only name that I'm familiar with in dispatches that was used was Kaznjenicka Bojna. This is dated, if I may comment on this order or this report?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Go ahead, sir.

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO GLASNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is dated, I believe, the 20th of June, 1993. The first report.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Exhibit P469?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO GLASNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The last four digits are 6051.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Sorry. There is -- there should be a P number, sir, on the document if you can find the exhibit, it says Exhibit P and the number unless they've come apart, I believe it's the number the document the sheet that's come apart underneath that one I believe I can see from -- the usher can help you.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters comment the witness had just quoted the number on the original and he was correct, 6051, that was the number on the original document.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This action on Boksevica I can speak my unit was in Boksevica, because I was there. I mentioned the previous testimony. And I can name the units engaged when we tactically withdrew from Boksevica. There was a tactical withdrawal which I led. And that was in the seventh month of 1993. So that is the only time that my units were on the Boksevica plateau.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Mr. President I see it's about time for the break and I believe we will not get a further answer so if you could like to break here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I'm just curious to know how long you will take in your cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: I expect to finish it but it will still take at least 35 to 40 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. We will break. We will resume at quarter to 6.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Scott.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Mr. President, [Microphone not activated].

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Mr. President, just so the Chamber knows I'm making an effort. I have skipped over a few topics so that we can hopefully finish as soon as possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Sir, I believe you testified that it was in the winter of 2000 that you first agreed to be a witness for Mr. Naletilic; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO GLASNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Krsnik contacted me about a year and a half ago.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And I believe that you testified yesterday that initially or at some point this was through, I think it was your word, intermediary. Who was that?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO GLASNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was actually my driver.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Who was that?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO GLASNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Popic.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Can you give us his full name, please?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO GLASNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Jozo.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Jozo Popic. Is that his first and last name?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO GLASNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: He's your driver or was your driver in your position as assistant or an adviser to the Minister of Defence?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO GLASNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was my driver for the last year of the war, from October, 1994, until actually October 1994 until November, 1995 and the following years after in increments.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And if you know, how was it that Mr. Krsnik and Mr. Popic had come to be in communication with each other?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO GLASNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There is a number I leave when I'm not available at work, a Mobitel number and he was more or less a message service, he was more or less an adjutant, not just a driver.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And through this Mr. Popic, then, did you ever direct contact with Mr. Krsnik as you said about 18 months ago?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO GLASNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And where was that?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO GLASNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In Siroki Brijeg at the restaurant, at the local sports centre.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And your testimony is, sir, that you agreed at that time to be a witness for Mr. Naletilic?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO GLASNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I agreed over the years, because I was approached by other defence council to be a witness for other individuals. For example, a character witness for General Blaskic and others, from 1997 on. This was not the only request.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: All right. And thank you for that, sir, but my question remains, at that contact with Mr. Krsnik, you agreed to be a witness for Mr. Naletilic, correct?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO GLASNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Now, you said the second time you had contact with Mr. Krsnik about being a witness was in February of this year, 2002; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO GLASNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I had not heard from him since, yes, since that time, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And please think hard, sir, and help the Judges. When in February was it that Mr. Krsnik contacted you? Was it in early February, mid-February, or approximately when?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO GLASNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I contacted Mr. Krsnik, not vice versa.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: When did you contact Mr. Krsnik in February?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO GLASNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The exact date, it was several days after returning from The Hague.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And -- all right. If you'll give me a moment, sir?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO GLASNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe the end of February, February 26th. I don't recall the exact date. It was several days after reading the statement and making my decision.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Sir, you returned from The Hague via Schipol, to Sarajevo on the 1st of March, 2002; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO GLASNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that was the date, if that's -- I can't recall the exact date. I was here in February for four or five days.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And how long was it, then, after your return to Sarajevo that you contacted Mr. Krsnik?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO GLASNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was several days later. It was after reading the statement that was given to me by the Tribunal.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: So prior to the time that you had -- you rejected or refused to sign the statement that you had given, you had contacted Mr. Krsnik and you had talked about the statement with him; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO GLASNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's incorrect. I think your sequence is a little mixed up, sir. I gave the --

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Go ahead. Please, maybe restate it, sir, maybe one of us misunderstood -- communicated. You said that after returning from The Hague, on approximately the 1st of March, some couple of days or so after that, you had contact with Mr. Krsnik. Now, we agree on that, correct?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO GLASNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's not exactly the sequence of events.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Please tell us.

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO GLASNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As for the time frame, I can given you the sequence of events, but exact dates at the moment I'm not certain of.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Please give us the sequence of events.

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO GLASNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was -- from the beginning, I was contacted by a member of the Tribunal, ICTY, in -- before Christmas of 19 -- or 2001, before the new year, and he wished -- well the first information I got is that someone from UNPROFOR wished to speak to me. I returned the call and the individual introduced himself and I realised he was from ICTY and not UNPROFOR and he asked me when a meeting would be appropriate and I left that up to his initiative.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Sir, I'm sorry --

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO GLASNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I'm getting.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: I've represented to the Chamber, I've committed to the Chamber, sir, that I would try to finish you in the next half hour or so?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO GLASNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because of his work load that was put off until the exacts time we met was in Sarajevo on the 9th floor of the ICTY building in Sarajevo and there were two members present and they wished to -- they basically asked me if I wanted to give a statement to the ICTY. I agreed to that, and as previously in the testimony, I also mentioned that -- they requested the entry be done in The Hague and not in Sarajevo for logistical reasons. I came here on a date which you have, which I don't have in front of me here, the exact date of the interview escapes me.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Sir, I can represent to you that you arrived at Schipol on the 25th of February, 2002.

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO GLASNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was after my birthday, I recall that summer. And I gave the interview. The logistical part of writing the interview was not finished here. I was asked to look at the interview and sign it in Sarajevo on a agreed upon date and that date you may also have, when I delivered that letter, I believe the several days after writing that letter I contacted Mr. Krsnik.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: All right, sir. Let's go back then. You told us yesterday in your testimony that you saw Mr. Krsnik a second time, or contacted, had communication with him, a second time in February 2002. Now, is that true or was that a misunderstanding?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO GLASNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's a misunderstanding. Following the sequence of events not the dates and I mentioned to you that I saw Mr. Krsnik several days after reading the witness statement and after delivering that letter to the ICTY after reading the statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: All right. And isn't it true, sir, that in the course of your -- all of your dealings with the representatives of the Office of the Prosecutor, that you were treated in a professional and courteous manner?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO GLASNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, depends on your, I think, connotation of courteous and proper. I could add something here without offending any one here in the Tribunal.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Please go ahead, sir.

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO GLASNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: My service in the correctional department of province of Alberta aside, I'm not a legal expert. Without lengthening this any further my decade in Bosnia-Herzegovina I had an open door policy. I worked hand in hand with the military organisations there, with the NGOs and I saw no reason not to speak to the people from the Tribunal and there were two reasons I spoke to the Tribunal. The first main reason was the picture that I had formed of the picture that was being represented, that I'd seen in the paper and the media of what happened in Bosnia-Herzegovina did not correspond to my experience during that decade. The second reason was, naturally, I was interested in my status with the ICTY during that period.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And I come back to my question, sir. You were treated in all respects in a professional and courteous manner and in fact, sir, isn't it true that up until the time that you refused to sign your statement on about the I believe it was about the 12th of March, just a few weeks ago, you had in fact quite cordial and friendly and cooperative dealings with the representatives of the Office of the Prosecutor and you were treated with respect and courteously, correct?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO GLASNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The cooperation was there, but again I say the main bone of contention was the witness statement itself and I explained why I didn't sign it in the letter.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: We will come to the letter, sir. Isn't it true that when you raised your concerns about the draft statement -- and let's get the facts straight here. You indeed did come to The Hague, not only after you agreed to it, but after the Minister of Defence of Bosnia-Herzegovina agreed to allow to you come here?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO GLASNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I asked for his permission, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And he gave it?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO GLASNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he did.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And in fact, the Office of the Prosecutor asked for his permission and he gave it. You came to The Hague, you were interviewed for several days, you were absolutely correct, the statement could not be prepared, typed, processed by the time you left The Hague. You returned home. The representatives of the Office of the Prosecutor returned or came -- travelled to Sarajevo on approximately the 11th of March, 2002, and gave you that statement and, in fact, gave it to you that you could take it with you and you could review it at your leisure and make any changes or additions that you wanted, correct?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO GLASNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would like to correct a few details in your statement. First of all, I was asked to come here incognito, and I did not want to come here incognito because I have nothing to hide. The second detail is, I asked them to ask the Minister of Defence to write a letter, because I wanted him to be aware that I was coming here.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And they did?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO GLASNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they did.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: All right. You came here, you gave a statement, you gave an interview, they came to The Hague, excuse me they left The Hague, came to Sarajevo on the 11th of March, gave you the statement, correct?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO GLASNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they did.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Told you to take it with you, review it at your leisure, and make any changes or additions that you wanted, isn't that true?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO GLASNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: You next saw the representatives of the Office of the Prosecutor on the 13th of March, two days later, and that is the time when you refused to sign your statement, correct?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO GLASNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And is it not true, sir, that throughout that meeting, you were once again urged to rewrite the statement, make any changes or additions that you cared to make and repeatedly invited to do that, isn't that true?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO GLASNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, sir, I'd like to add something here.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Well, first answer my question. I'll let you add something but first answer my question, please. Were you not repeatedly offered the opportunity to rewrite the statement in any way that you wanted?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO GLASNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the beginning, no. I was told to leave. The first -- the first -- the first statement from one of the gentlemen, which I don't want to name by name, perhaps his job is on the line, is -- his first comment to me was, "Why don't you leave right now?" And I said, "I certainly will."

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Wait a minute, sir. When was this said?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO GLASNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was said as soon as I made my statement that I would not sign this. I made a comment that I would not sign the witness statement for the reasons I mentioned in my letter. There are 64 letters or there are 64 pages to that statement or more, I believe.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: That's correct, sir, and you told us that most of you what said was left out and yet it's a 64 page statement?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO GLASNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, I firmly believe that a witness should be credible and objective, which I tried to be in the statement, and not a chess piece on a chess board, which is how I felt after that whole after reading only the first 8 pages of the statement. There were so many inaccuracies, there were so many false assumptions and the statement was worded -- every answer was worded so were not my words. Again I mention to you the preceding part of the statement which said this. This is a substantially verbatim statement which again I mentioned at the beginning of this statement -- my statement two days ago. I do not understand what that means. The word style was used. This for me is a verbatim statement is what I'm saying here. Not the statements that I gave. That's why I refused to sign it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: I'm not sure, sir. You said are you refusing to sign it because it was not a verbatim statement? I'm not sure what you just said?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO GLASNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, again in the letter I'll repeat what I said, it was inaccurate. It was leading. It formulated theory and a thesis which I do not accept. In principle, it does not correspond to my view of what happened here from 1992 to 1995 and after perhaps, if there were any questions dealing with after. That is why I did not sign the statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Sir, I don't know of any verbatim statement of any sort except perhaps the one that's made in a courtroom with a reporter taking down. This is a statement. So, is it not true, and is it not accurate for the person to represent to you that it was a substantially verbatim statement? Is that not in fact an accurate description of the statement?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO GLASNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I will remind you again, sir, that the main points which I accentuated, which I found important in that statement were deleted.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And did you offer to add those statements when you were repeatedly asked to make any changes or additions that you wanted to make?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO GLASNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not, sir, because I saw from the line of questioning, the way the answers were formulated, what the thesis was of the people that questioned me and I had no intention of doing someone's homework by rewriting 64 pages of statement again.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: I'd like the witness to please be shown Exhibit 921: I'd like you to direct your attention, sir, first of all, to page 36?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't see the relevancy of this questioning and my objection is that again in the cross-examination, he has explained once again, and I'm glad that the Chamber has heard, under conditions how statements are taken, how this is being done and that now the statement is being presented which was totally refuted. Are we going to elicit now comments on this statement? What is to be attained with that? In what sense is that relevant?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Krsnik, during the direct examination, I think you mentioned this issue first and showed us the letter written by this witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: You aroused our interest in this very matter. We want to know what is in the statement, and we want to know what he is examined about.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Page 36, sir, at the top part of the page the questions are actually numbered in this particular statement or draft statement, I will say. Question 218: You were asked the question, and again substantially verbatim form, "As brigade commander what did you do in order to ensure compliance with LOAC, the law of -- to be honest at the moment, the abbreviation -- Law of Armed Conflict -- and GC, Geneva Convention by your personnel. Answer: As stated I discussed this issue with Siljeg several times at the operative zone level, also made this known to my battalion commanders. My awareness, LOAY and GC was not so much familiarity with the exact wording of law but more based on my own moral standards and a sense of what was right and what was wrong. This was only common sense." Now, isn't that exactly what you testified to this Chamber today?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO GLASNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No different from what I said on this statement. If I can add something?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Now, sir, I only have a few minutes of time and if the Chamber would like to hear from you, then you can extend the time. I can direct your attention, please, to page 45. Question 296?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: Just a moment, can I say something to you or can I ask something, Mr. Scott? Isn't it normal for an exhibit to be a clean copy? Who has put all those comments and marks and that sort of thing here? I hope you would explain that to us first before we actually look at the --

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: My mistake Judge Clark. You're absolutely right of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Sir, when you look at Exhibit 9212 and the notation that is have been put on here, the circling of sections on page 45, the words "total B/S" circled around question 300, question mark, who made those annotations, sir?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO GLASNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did. If I may answer the question in --

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Sorry, do we --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: Judge Lieu appears to have a clean copy and I have a decorated one.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: There is two, there is 920, which is the clean version and 921, which is the copy the witness annotated.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: Thank you, that explains things.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: I should have made that clear at the outset and I apologise.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Could I please finish answering my questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: I'll just answer this way, Mr. President. I will not finish tonight if we have long, continuous non-responsive answers on these matters.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, witness, you may answer the question in a very concise way.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Sir, I'll be brief. The statements was so full of inaccuracies and fallacies that I circled this myself and on page 45 you will see such one circled statement which says excuse my language, "total BS." All 64 pages are full of this.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Sir, on page 45, one of the ones -- one of the items you circled question 296 you were asked a question about the preparation by the HVO, but in fact, you gave an answer about preparations by the ABiH during mid-April, 1993 there had been an incident where the ABiH had attacked one of our barracks and this resulted in the death of 26 -- sorry, HVO soldiers, et cetera. Now, sir, once again isn't that exactly what you told the Chamber in the course of your testimony the last two days?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO GLASNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's common knowledge, sir, that the fighting in Mostar started, I know this from dispatches, is when soldiers of the HVO were attacked in the same barracks they shared with the army BH or the MOS and they were killed. The details of that operation I'm sure Mr. Krsnik knows better than I do. I see no inconsistency with this.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Exactly, exactly. Page 46, question 302: This is the only last example I will give. It's just talking about the use of prisoners in forced labour in connection or coming from the Heliodrom. I will simply go to it the last line. Does the statement not say, "It was further known that Muslim forces were subjecting Croat prisoners of war to this illegal treatment resulting in the death of many Croat prisoners"? Now, sir, isn't that a balanced presentation of exactly what you said?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO GLASNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, it's not so much the details in the -- it's the thesis of the whole statement, sir, which I do not agree with and that is why I refused to sign.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And you were repeatedly, sir, given the opportunity to write the statement in any way you wished and of course you know that the investigators that you conversed with, you can certainly come and testify about what happened as well?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO GLASNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm fully aware of that fact.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: You -- the letter that is marked as excuse me -- the letter -- and if it will assist you, sir, the usher may, if you don't still have it, the usher may show you Exhibit D1/330, your 12th of March, 2002 letter. Now, sir, please tell the Chamber after leaving the Sarajevo office of the ICTY on the 11th of March of this year, having been given a copy of the draft statement to take with you and to review, when did you first come in contact with, forgive me with the first name, Ivan Jurilj and Mr. Miro Grbavac?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO GLASNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe it was the next day. The exact date is shortly after reading the agreement or reading the statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And where was this letter prepared, sir?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO GLASNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was prepared in the Ministry of Defence, and in the sector for the train and equip programme of the federation army or the Ministry of Defence level, I should say.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Whose office, in whose office was it prepared?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO GLASNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In Mr. Grbavac's office.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Who typed it or word-processed it?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO GLASNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Ivan Jurilj did. I dictated the wording and he typed it for me.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Who is Mr. Ivan Jurilj?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO GLASNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Uric. He's the operative in the office, the MPRI office, in Sarajevo, the assistant to Mr. Miro Grbavac.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Mr. Grbavac's assistant?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO GLASNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And had you had dealings with him before this occasion?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO GLASNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I had previously, yes, but briefly he was a member of my unit before, this was in the 1st Guards Brigade, I believe, five years ago.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Now, did you know this man, Grbavac, before 2002?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO GLASNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: How did you know him?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO GLASNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was the -- he was in the G3 sector of the HVO headquarters, the training sector, from 1998 on, I believe.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: In what general location. In Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO GLASNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, at the time I was in Posusje. It was earlier.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And how long had you known Mr. Grbavac prior to the 12th of March, 2002?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO GLASNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Since approximately 1997 or perhaps earlier.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And can you tell me, sir, looking, directing your attention to the -- well let me back up. Did you show Mr. Jurilj, my apology, I have trouble with that one and Mr. Grbavac, did you show them the draft statement before this letter was prepared?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO GLASNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We discussed the statement. I voiced my disagreements with what was written and my reasons for not signing it. I showed other people the statement, however, in the intelligence sector of the Ministry of Defence, people that I work with.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Who in the intelligence sector did you show it to?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO GLASNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was Mr. Peric, I believe or one of his associates in the Ministry of Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Who is Mr. Peric?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO GLASNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He's one of the members, operatives employed in the security sector in the Ministry of Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: You say he's an operative. What does he do?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO GLASNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's self explanatory. His concern is security and information gathering.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Is he a field intelligence operative? Is that what you're telling us?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO GLASNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Field? He's more or less, not so much a field operative but he's an analyst.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Do you know him before that time?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO GLASNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: When you were sitting in Mr. Grbavac's office writing this letter?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I? Your Honours, may I now -- will you please enlighten me, what does this investigation lead to about who wrote this letter, who typed it, about these persons and how relevant is this to our case? This looks like -- this smacks of an investigation to me, but we do not know about what.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, I think this matter is closely related to the credibility of this witness, since this issue was mentioned during the direct examination and the cross-examination, we have to know what's going on there. Yes, Mr. Scott.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Sir, as you sat Mr. Grbavac's office or presence, I don't know if you were sitting or not, as were you in Mr. Grbavac's office preparing this letter, who picked in the very first line, who picked the words "so-called"?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO GLASNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I dictated every word of this statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Every word is your word?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO GLASNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Now, isn't it correct, sir, that then you -- you had you indicated to the representatives of the Office of the Prosecutor on the 12th of March -- I'm sorry, on the 13th of March, I think now, yes, that you would not sign the statement, they again repeatedly invited you to rewrite the statement in any way you wished, then you saw them again on Friday, the 15th of March, 2002, primarily for the purpose of providing, if you will, the travel papers in connection with your trip to The Hague so you could be properly reimbursed; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO GLASNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I was asked to bring over my airline ticket.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And approximately what time did you leave the Sarajevo field office on Friday, the 15th of March, after doing that?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO GLASNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't recall the exact -- the time or the place or the -- I can't recall the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Not exact minutes sir, but was it the morning, the afternoon, evening, early evening?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO GLASNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe it was the afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Mr. President I'm going to direct the Chamber's attention now to, not to put on the ELMO, I'm not going to mention any names at the moment, but Exhibit P923, if that could be given to the witness, again not to be broadcast at this moment. Mr. President, perhaps we could go into private session just for a minute.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, we will go to the private session, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I'm sorry to interrupt you, witness, you may answer that question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I had no certainty or knowledge that I was going to testify here at this trial. I was contacted by Mr. Krsnik two days before my arrival here, and in all fairness to Mr. Krsnik, it was a bit short notice. I had other serious personal problems to contend with, but I assumed this was the most important, and I came here on short notice. For over a year and a half or since I met Mr. -- The first contact, I did not truthfully expect to be called here as a witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Mr. President, I am finishing. I have a couple of more questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Sir, isn't it true that this Miro Grbavac is the head of an organisation called the Croat defence council or HVO volunteers and veterans of the homeland war often known as the UDIVDR.

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO GLASNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think, sir, you ever the wrong Grbavac. There are two Grbavac's. The one you're referring to is nicknamed "Titan" and he's head of the so-called association of volunteers or the name escapes me. There are two different individuals, two different names. The Miro Grbavac, I mentioned was an ex-JNA officer, artillery officer employed now in the NPRI sector in the federation.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Are you telling the Chamber that your being involved in this statement or rejecting this statement had nothing to do with this organisation, the association of volunteers and veterans of the homeland war?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO GLASNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And are you aware, sir, that Mladen Naletilic, Tuta, is the honorary lifetime president of that organisation?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO GLASNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not aware that he's a lifetime -- no I'm not aware of this fact. I never attended one meeting of this organisation.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Mr. President, thank you for your patience. In the interests of time, I will conclude. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, re-examination, Mr. Krsnik?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I'd only like to use three documents, the same ones that the Prosecutor used. Could the witness be shown first P299.4? Re-examined by Mr. Krsnik

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Let me tell you witness the document -- I won't want to be cautioned by the Chamber, the defence's position is that it does not recognise these documents. We challenge them. Will you please look at this. Does this document have a signature and a -- no, sorry, first question, did you receiver this on the 4th of August, 1994, this documentation, this commendation from the Minister of Defence?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO GLASNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If I may mention the precautions taken against the abuse of the system of writing orders and requests within the commands of the HVO military commands, every unit had a stamp with its unit emblem that was kept under lock and key it was used only by three or four people authorised to use that stamp. I didn't see these stamps on any of these documents. Also in my headquarters, there were only three people that I delegated that were allowed to sign any order or request when they represented me as a -- in a liaison with another unit so these -- this is not the way I would have done things, nor can I certify or say anything about these orders that were shown to me. Whether they are accurate or inaccurate but this to me is a -- it's highly informal and it could be -- I've never seen anything like this.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
